subject: Chemistry
description: Oxidation numbers / states — assignment rules, examples in elements/compounds, redox identification, calculation in complex compounds.

questions.stem: The OXIDATION NUMBER of an element in its FREE/elemental form is:
questions.explanation: OXIDATION NUMBER (oxidation state) RULES (memorize): (1) ELEMENT in PURE/FREE form (atomic or molecular): oxidation number = ZERO. Examples: Na (s), O₂ (g), N₂, Cl₂, S₈, P₄, Fe (s), C (graphite). All atoms in these molecules: ON = 0. (2) IONS — equals charge of ion: Na⁺ → +1; Cl⁻ → −1; Mg²⁺ → +2; O²⁻ → −2. (3) HYDROGEN: typically +1 (H₂O: H = +1); EXCEPTION: −1 in metal hydrides (NaH, MgH₂). (4) OXYGEN: typically −2 (in oxides, H₂O); EXCEPTIONS: −1 in peroxides (H₂O₂, Na₂O₂); +2 in OF₂. (5) FLUORINE always −1 (most electronegative). (6) HALOGENS (Cl, Br, I) typically −1 in binary compounds; can be +1, +3, +5, +7 with O. (7) ALKALI METALS (Group 1): always +1 (Na, K, Li). (8) ALKALINE EARTH (Group 2): always +2 (Mg, Ca, Ba). (9) SUM RULE: total oxidation states must equal NET CHARGE of compound/ion. KEY APPLICATIONS: (a) IDENTIFYING REDOX REACTIONS (oxidation = increase in ON; reduction = decrease). (b) BALANCING REDOX EQUATIONS. (c) Predicting stability of oxidation states. UPSC angle: redox is staple of NEET, NCERT Class 11, JEE-Main. PYQ FREQUENCY: ON of element-in-element form in NEET, JEE-Main 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of S in SO₄²⁻ (sulfate)?
questions.explanation: Apply SUM RULE: total oxidation numbers = NET charge of ion. SO₄²⁻ has net charge −2. EQUATION: S + 4(O) = −2; with O = −2 (standard rule), 4 × (−2) = −8; S + (−8) = −2 → S = +6. So sulfur is in OXIDATION STATE +6 in sulfate. KEY S OXIDATION STATES: −2 (H₂S, sulfides like Na₂S); 0 (S₈, elemental); +2 (S₂Cl₂); +4 (SO₂, SO₃²⁻ sulfite); +6 (SO₃, SO₄²⁻ sulfate, H₂SO₄ sulfuric acid). KEY METHOD for finding ON in compounds: (1) Apply known rules: O = −2, H = +1 (with exceptions). (2) Set unknown element's ON as variable. (3) Balance: sum of all ON × atom count = total charge (0 for neutral; ion charge for ion). (4) Solve. PRACTICE — find ON of: (a) Cl in HClO₃: H + Cl + 3O = 0 → 1 + Cl + (−6) = 0 → Cl = +5. (b) N in NO₃⁻: N + 3(−2) = −1 → N = +5. (c) Mn in KMnO₄: K + Mn + 4(−2) = 0 → 1 + Mn + (−8) = 0 → Mn = +7. (d) Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇: 2(+1) + 2Cr + 7(−2) = 0 → 2 + 2Cr − 14 = 0 → Cr = +6. (e) Fe in FeCl₃: Fe + 3(−1) = 0 → Fe = +3 (ferric/Fe³⁺). PYQ FREQUENCY: ON-calculation problems in NEET, JEE-Main 2-3× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests systematic application of rules.

options.option_text: Loss of electrons / gain in ON
Gain of electrons / loss in ON

questions.explanation: OXIDATION (modern definition): LOSS of ELECTRONS by an atom or ion → INCREASE in oxidation number. REDUCTION: GAIN of electrons → DECREASE in oxidation number. MNEMONIC: OIL RIG ('Oxidation Is Loss; Reduction Is Gain' — of electrons). Or LEO GER ('Loss of Electrons = Oxidation; Gain of Electrons = Reduction'). REDOX REACTIONS: oxidation + reduction occur TOGETHER (one substance loses e⁻, another gains). Cannot have one without other. EXAMPLES: (1) Combustion: C + O₂ → CO₂. C goes from 0 to +4 (oxidized); O₂ goes from 0 to −2 (reduced). (2) Rusting: Fe (0) → Fe³⁺ (+3); O₂ → O²⁻. (3) Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂; C reduced (+4 → 0); O oxidized (−2 → 0). (4) Battery: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu; Zn oxidized, Cu²⁺ reduced. HISTORICAL DEFINITIONS — broader: (a) ORIGINAL: oxidation = ADDITION of OXYGEN. Reduction = REMOVAL of OXYGEN. (b) EXTENDED: oxidation = REMOVAL of HYDROGEN. (c) MODERN ELECTRON-TRANSFER: above. Modern definition is most general (covers reactions without O or H). KEY INDIA APPLICATIONS: (a) RUSTING — major economic loss. (b) Steel-making (Bessemer process). (c) Mineral extraction. UPSC angle: redox in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT Class 11. PYQ FREQUENCY: redox definition in NEET 1-2× per paper, NCERT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: In H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide), the oxidation number of OXYGEN is:
questions.explanation: EXCEPTION TO O = −2 RULE: in PEROXIDES (H₂O₂, Na₂O₂, BaO₂), OXYGEN is in oxidation state −1. Why? Two oxygen atoms are connected by a single O−O bond; each oxygen has gained only ONE electron from the other partner, not two. Apply sum: H₂O₂ neutral. 2H = 2 × (+1) = +2. 2O = total = −2. So each O = −1. STANDARD RULES revisited: (a) O = −2 in most oxides (CO₂, H₂O, MgO). (b) O = −1 in PEROXIDES (H₂O₂, Na₂O₂). (c) O = −1/2 in SUPEROXIDES (KO₂, RbO₂). (d) O = +2 in OF₂ (oxygen fluoride — F more electronegative than O). (e) O = +1 in O₂F₂. (f) O = 0 in elemental O₂. PEROXIDES uses + properties: H₂O₂ is OXIDIZING agent (releases O atom: H₂O₂ → H₂O + ½O₂); used as DISINFECTANT (3% solution for wounds), HAIR BLEACH (~6%), ROCKET propellant (~98% concentration), pulp/paper bleaching, water treatment. INDIA: H₂O₂ used widely in textile industry (cotton bleaching), dental treatments. SUPEROXIDES form between Group 1 metals + O₂: very reactive; KO₂ used in OXYGEN GENERATORS (submarines, space stations) — reacts with CO₂ to release O₂. PYQ FREQUENCY: O = −1 in peroxide is a NEET, JEE-Main top trap — 1× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests rule-exceptions awareness.

questions.stem: In NH₃ (ammonia), oxidation number of NITROGEN is:
questions.explanation: Apply RULES: NH₃ is neutral (charge = 0). H = +1 (standard). So N + 3(+1) = 0 → N = −3. So N is in oxidation state −3 in ammonia. KEY N OXIDATION STATES (memorize): −3 (NH₃ ammonia, NH₄⁺ ammonium); −2 (N₂H₄ hydrazine); −1 (NH₂OH hydroxylamine); 0 (N₂ elemental); +1 (N₂O nitrous oxide, 'laughing gas'); +2 (NO nitric oxide); +3 (HNO₂ nitrous acid, NO₂⁻ nitrite); +4 (NO₂ nitrogen dioxide); +5 (HNO₃ nitric acid, NO₃⁻ nitrate). NITROGEN's RANGE of OXIDATION STATES (−3 to +5) is the WIDEST among common elements — nitrogen is incredibly versatile in chemistry. AMMONIA NH₃: (a) Strong base, accepts proton → NH₄⁺. (b) Industrial: HABER PROCESS (N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃) at high T, P, with Fe catalyst — billions of tonnes/year for fertilizers. (c) UREA, ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate fertilizers all from ammonia. (d) INDIA: ~25 million tonnes urea/year (largest urea producer); fertilizer subsidies major govt expenditure. UPSC angle: AGRICULTURE — fertilizer policy, nitrogen pollution (excess runoff causes algal blooms, eutrophication). NCERT Class 12 mentions N's variable oxidation states extensively. NUCLEAR: N₂O₄ is rocket fuel oxidizer. PYQ FREQUENCY: N oxidation states in NEET, JEE-Main 2-3× per paper.

questions.stem: In KMnO₄ (potassium permanganate, an oxidizing agent), oxidation number of Mn is:
questions.explanation: Apply: K + Mn + 4O = 0. K = +1 (Group 1), O = −2 (standard). 1 + Mn + 4(−2) = 0 → 1 + Mn − 8 = 0 → Mn = +7. So Mn is in +7 state — HIGHEST possible for manganese. WHY KMnO₄ is a STRONG OXIDIZER: it ACCEPTS electrons readily (gets REDUCED), going from +7 → +2 (in acidic conditions) or +4 (in neutral/alkaline) — large electron-gain. COMMON Mn OXIDATION STATES: 0 (Mn metal); +2 (MnSO₄, Mn²⁺ salts — pale pink); +3; +4 (MnO₂ — used in dry cells); +6 (MnO₄²⁻ manganate); +7 (KMnO₄ — DEEP PURPLE solution, characteristic). KMnO₄ USES: (1) DISINFECTANT — for wounds, skin infections, water purification (potency known as 'Condy's Crystals' historically). (2) BLEACHING agent — paper, textiles. (3) WATER TREATMENT — removes iron, manganese, hydrogen sulfide. (4) ANALYTICAL — TITRATION (deep purple → colourless when reduced; SELF-INDICATING). (5) REDOX TITRATION standard reagent. (6) Anti-fungal in soaks for athlete's foot. INDIA INDUSTRIAL: KMnO₄ is a major export item (India is leading producer; Tamil Nadu has largest plants). 2014 export: India accounted for ~70% of global KMnO₄ supply. UPSC angle: industry-specific facts in PT general awareness; environmental impact of manganese mining. PYQ FREQUENCY: KMnO₄ oxidation state in NEET, JEE-Main 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: In K₂Cr₂O₇ (potassium dichromate), what is the oxidation number of Cr?
questions.explanation: Apply rules: K = +1, O = −2; total charge = 0 (neutral compound). 2(+1) + 2(Cr) + 7(−2) = 0 → 2 + 2Cr − 14 = 0 → 2Cr = 12 → Cr = +6. So chromium is in +6 oxidation state in dichromate. KEY Cr OXIDATION STATES: 0 (Cr metal); +2 (CrO, Cr²⁺ salts — blue); +3 (Cr₂O₃, Cr³⁺ salts — green); +6 (CrO₃, K₂Cr₂O₇, Na₂CrO₄ — orange/yellow). K₂Cr₂O₇ (Potassium DICHROMATE) — orange-red crystalline solid; STRONG OXIDIZING AGENT in acidic medium: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O. USES: (1) ANALYTICAL — REDOX titrations (e.g., COD test for water quality — chemical oxygen demand). (2) LEATHER tanning. (3) DYES + pigments. (4) WOOD preservatives. (5) Photography (historical). RELATED: K₂CrO₄ (chromate) — yellow; in alkaline solution. Equilibrium: 2 CrO₄²⁻ (yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) + H₂O. Color shifts indicate pH. SAFETY: Cr⁶⁺ compounds are HIGHLY TOXIC + CARCINOGENIC (Erin Brockovich case in USA — Cr-6 in groundwater Hinkley, California). India: hexavalent chromium pollution from leather industry (Tamil Nadu, Kanpur — major problem; tanneries restricted under SC orders). UPSC angle: industrial pollution + environmental law (Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Environment Protection Act 1986). PYQ FREQUENCY: Cr oxidation states in NEET, JEE-Main 1× per cycle.
